newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX PV electric futures settle higher, COB lower.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX PV electric futures settle higher, COB lower.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled mixed Tuesday in another quiet, rangebound session amid a soft cash market in the West.
"It's another boring day," a Houston-based power marketer said.
September Palo Verde (PV) futures settled up eight cents at $30.52 a megawatt hour, midway between the day's high at $30.70 and day's low at $30.15.
October PV finished up 16 cents at $23.76. Most deferred PV contracts were inactive.
Market sources said a rally in natural gas futures lent psychological support for PV prices.
"It's kind of hard not to buy (gas futures) if they're driving up you're fuel cost," another marketer said.
The NYMEX September Henry Hub natgas contract settled up 10.2 cents at $2.528 per million British thermal units.
September California-Oregon Border (COB) settled down 23 cents at $22.76 a MWh after bouncing in a 30 cent range.
October COB finished unchanged at $22.55. Other COB months ended down 10 to up 15 cents.
Physical power prices in the West were generally softer Tuesday despite news of outages of two of fossil fueled power units in the Southwest.
Firm peak power prices at PV fell more than $2.00 to $27.50-28.50 a MWh, while those at COB were steady at $18.00-19.00.
A 540 megawatt (MW) unit at the San Juan coal-fired plant in New Mexico was said to be off line due to tube leak, but a time estimate for the outage was not available.
A 750 MW natural gas-fired unit at the Ormond Beach power plant near Los Angeles remained out of service for maintenance work after being shut Friday. There is no estimate restart time for the unit.

In other western electricity news, the 3,800 MW AC segment of the Pacific Intertie was scheduled to be curtailed to 2,950 MW between 0800-1600 PDT through Friday, while the DC line will be limited to 2,360 over the same period.
A high pressure ridge building in the West was expected to heat the region's temperatures three to seven degrees Fahrenheit above normal through Friday, meteorologists said.

In its latest six to 10 day forecast, Weather Services Corp said temperatures would average below normal along the coastal region, near normal further inland and above normal in the eastern part of the Southwest.
NYMEX estimated 459 PV and 225 COB contracts were sold.
